═══ SESSION: 34 CLOSED · e3cd MERGED · S6 PROVEN AND RESCOPED · 8h AUTONOMOUS WINDOW OPENED ═══

## THE SCOPE RULING THAT UNBLOCKED S6 — the single most important thing in this log
OPERATOR: "LLMs are non-deterministic. Expecting two runs to produce identical results is unrealistic
AND BEYOND THE SCOPE OF THIS EPIC. The scope is that the same PAYLOADS reach the LLM and the LLM has
the same TOOLS available, regardless of model and provider. COMPARING MODELS AGAINST ONE ANOTHER IS
OUT OF SCOPE."
Before this, S6 was UNPROVABLE: `parity.py:107` fails on ANY nonzero decision_flips ("must be 0", no
margin), the 3 flips are genuine and reproducible, and no re-score removes them. 0d76's ACs were
retargeted to payload/tool parity; the flip/agreement numbers are now INFORMATIONAL.
0d76 IS NOW EVIDENCED: payload parity (system/messages/tools byte-identical; model id the only
differing field), tool parity (6 tools identical), capability difference MODEL-driven not
PROVIDER-driven (temperature withdrawn from opus on BOTH providers), provider-clean 84/84.
Captured at the provider boundary with ZERO network calls.

## OPERATOR DECISIONS IN FORCE
* Cutover authorised IF no known Bedrock-IMPLEMENTATION bugs — already true; every open bug is harness
  or provider-agnostic caching. What holds eb6e is the bar confirmation, not a Bedrock defect.
* HOLD 0d76 open + HOLD cutover until Bedrock confirmed. 0d76 may CLOSE once its stack merges and the
  rescoped ACs verify. eb6e still will not start: 1aa2 also blocks it.
* NO Anthropic-vs-Anthropic noise-floor run. Cost-conscious about LARGE EVAL BATCHES ONLY — subagents
  and live validation calls are free rein. IF AN AC BLOCKS CLOSURE, REMEDIATE IT TOWARD A NARROWLY
  SCOPED LIVE CALL rather than stalling or running a sweep.
* Submit scope: ONLY changes this session owns. `owner:self` returns OTHER sessions' changes under the
  shared RebarBotNava identity — filter by what you pushed.
* Budget guard: dev-only, off the critical path, NOT filed.

## MERGED / CLOSED
e3cd MERGED (1263). Closed this session: 5e75, 7a79, d5c7, 48b3, 77ed, df2c(duplicate), 5267, 8415,
c403, 1157. Epic 34 of 43.

## ON GERRIT — all rebased onto the two NEW gates, all pushed
1266-1271 (0d76 stack + 62ac + 635f) · 1277 043f · 1278 84aa · 1281 b718 · 1282 9ac2 · 1284 12e4

## TWO NEW CI GATES LANDED ON MAIN TODAY — run BOTH before any push
  python3 scripts/check_config_reads.py         # Config-read gate, ticket 6754
  python3 scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check   # env drift
THE CONFIG-READ GATE COST A FULL CI CYCLE ON THREE STACKS. Cause: the gate is NEW on main and invokes
`scripts/check_config_reads.py`; older branches DO NOT CONTAIN that script, and Gerrit CI runs the
TARGET branch's workflow — so it invoked a script absent from the tree. Pure base staleness; rebasing
fixes it. Always rebase before diagnosing a CI failure you cannot reproduce.
THE DRIFT GATE TRIPS ON LINE-NUMBER SHIFTS, not just new env vars — docs/env-vars.md records usages BY
LINE. Editing any file that reads an env var makes it stale.

## MISTAKES I MADE — all corrected, all worth not repeating
1. COUNT-BASED IDEMPOTENCY GUARDS SILENTLY SKIPPED TWO WRITES. `[ "$n" -ge 12 ]` exits early when the
   ticket already has more comments. Both operator DECISION records (0d76 hold, eb6e cutover hold)
   were reported as landed and had NOT been written. ALWAYS GUARD BY CONTENT, never by count.
2. READ ONE SIDE OF A BIDIRECTIONAL EDGE. `rebar show eb6e` lists only its OUTGOING `blocks -> 8625`;
   the incoming block lives on 0d76's record. I concluded eb6e was unblocked and dispatched an agent
   that could never have succeeded (review-plan fast-fails on a blocked ticket). Filed as 05cb.
3. PER-COMMIT GREENNESS. 1266 added a test reading an artifact added in 1268. Local runs tested the
   TIP so it looked green; CI tests EACH patchset. Fixed with a skip-if-absent guard, verified
   per-commit.
4. zsh does NOT word-split unquoted `$var`, so `set -- $spec` made six close attempts malformed.

## GERRIT BEHAVIOURS THAT LOOK LIKE FAILURES
* A TRIVIAL_REBASE COPIES A STALE -1 FORWARD and does NOT re-run CI. 1267 showed Verified-1 on PS2
  with no STARTED message. The tell is the absence of a CI run for that patch set. Comment `recheck`.
* Gerrit REWRITES SHAs on submit; re-derive refs by `rebar-ticket:` trailer afterwards.

## WHAT THE AGENTS PROVED (each corrected something I believed)
* df2c CLOSED AS DUPLICATE of 0347 — its agent disproved its own finished, green, mutation-checked
  work. 0347 keys on `gap_reason`, `review-error` was ALREADY in RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS, and 0347's
  coverage is a strict SUPERSET. A second mechanism at the vote decision point was NOT landed.
* 635f: my filed mechanism was WRONG. `parity.py:105` filters on `a.label` (the GOLD LABEL), not
  `decision` — so NO decision value exempts an errored pair, and changing fidelity_spot_eval.py:174
  is a NO-OP. The real defect is the missing `errored` guard at `:107`.
* f81d: the prescribed remedy is DISPROVEN. Both cache mechanisms mark AFTER the whole message list,
  so both sites are write-only BY CONSTRUCTION and the guard would be inert. My premise that
  coach_notes could hit the finders' warm entry is false — they diverge at the first system byte. ACs
  remediated; WON'T-FIX is now an explicitly acceptable outcome pending a value measurement.
* 62ac: the frontier false-accept "failure" was the INVERTED METRIC. Corrected: v1 0.214 vs v2 0.071 —
  Bedrock false-fires less than a THIRD as often and was being failed FOR THE IMPROVEMENT.
* b718/9ac2: found a SECOND poisoner — `install_stderr_handler()` setLevel(WARNING) on the shared
  `rebar` logger via `_cli.main()`, which 11 test files invoke in-process. Made the intermittent
  StopIteration DETERMINISTIC, then fixed it. Established BY INSTRUMENTATION that ZERO of the five
  negative caplog assertions were void. Corrected my "process-wide" claim: on pytest 9.1.1 the void
  window is ONE TEST PHASE.
* 12e4: stall aborts in 5.1s vs the 300s ceiling; a 2000 B/s dribble is NOT aborted and three cold
  80MB clones (88-101s) survive the defaults. The module split was FORCED (repo_snapshot 788/800).

## OSS COMPARISON OF THE LANDED SEAM — top findings, filed
* dd27 (NEW, in epic): the AGENTIC message tail is re-sent UNCACHED every turn — O(N^2) input cost,
  and INVISIBLE to our telemetry because the system block keeps cache_read nonzero so
  warn_if_cache_ineffective never fires. Both knobs already exist in pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1.
  PROVIDER ASYMMETRY IS THE TRAP: Bedrock has no `bedrock_cache` automatic key and REJECTS top-level
  cache_control (langchain#37042 regressed on exactly this).
* 7fe2 (NEW, in epic): a `gateway/*` provider signs as tier `first_class` because tier derives solely
  from base_url — misrepresents provenance in a SIGNED verdict. One-line fix.
* VINDICATED, no change: no-fallback-by-default (matches consensus; rebar's predicate is STRICTER than
  pydantic-ai's, which fails over on any 4xx incl. auth); the ":" separator (membership test beats
  maxsplit=1); LiteLLM rejection (its Bedrock id-sniffing produces a recurring bug cluster); tenacity
  transport; genai-prices; json-repair before validation.
* Model-class indirection: the community never converged on tiers, BUT rebar's slots are role
  assignments in practice (cf. Aider's --weak-model) and the usage log records class AND resolved
  model. Renaming would be churn, not a fix.
* CORROBORATION: the report independently found 4096 wrong for DEFAULT_MODEL (should be 1024) — which
  is exactly what e3cd fixed and merged.

## TICKETS FILED THIS SESSION
In epic: f81d, 635f, 12e4, e3cd, c403, 1aa2, dd27, 7fe2. Outside: 84aa, 043f, b718, 9ac2, 05cb, 5968,
851e, 62ac.

## THE CHAIN
  0d76 ─┐
        ├─blocks─→ eb6e ─blocks─→ 8625
  1aa2 ─┘
1aa2 is READY and UNBLOCKED — the only unblocked critical-path work. Agent running it now with live
gate authorisation. eb6e's alarm ALREADY EXISTS (S4b shipped it, verified live StateValue OK); its
Scope overstates the work and only the kill-switch runbook is genuinely new.
